Surgical Fire Risk Assessment And Prevention - Ecri Guidelines

FIRE TRIANGLE ASSESSMENT:

OXIDIZER: IGNITION SOURCE: FUEL:
☐ Oxygen (open delivery) ☐ Electrosurgical unit (ESU) ☐ Drapes
☐ Nitrous oxide ☐ Laser ☐ Prep solution
☐ Air ☐ Fiberoptic light source ☐ Patient hair
☐ Other: _________ ☐ Drills/burrs ☐ Gauze/sponges
☐ Defibrillator ☐ Tapes/dressings
☐ Other: _________ ☐ Endotracheal tube
☐ Other: _____

FIRE RISK LEVEL: Low ☐ Moderate ☐ High ☐

FIRE PREVENTION MEASURES:

☐ Alcohol-based prep dried completely before draping

☐ ESU in holster when not in use

☐ Laser on standby when not in use

☐ Minimize oxygen concentration (FiO2 <30% if possible)

☐ Wet sponges/gauze near ignition source

☐ Fire-resistant drapes used

☐ Fire risk discussed in time-out

FIRE RESPONSE PROCEDURES - R.A.C.E.:

R - Rescue/Remove patient from immediate danger

A - Alarm/Activate fire alarm

C - Contain/Close doors

E - Extinguish/Evacuate

FIRE RESPONSE - P.A.S.S. (for extinguisher use):

P - Pull the pin

A - Aim at base of fire

S - Squeeze the handle

S - Sweep from side to side

AIRWAY FIRE RESPONSE:

1. Remove endotracheal tube

2. Stop flow of all gases

3. Pour saline into airway

4. Remove burning materials

5. Re-establish airway

Surgical Site Infection (Ssi) Prevention Bundle - Cdc/Shea Guidelines

PRE-OPERATIVE MEASURES:

☐ Nasal decolonization (if MRSA carrier) ☐ Chlorhexidine bathing night before/morning of surgery
☐ Appropriate hair removal (clippers only, no razors)☐ Antimicrobial prophylaxis within 60 minutes of incision
☐ Screen for and treat remote infections ☐ Optimize glucose control (HbA1c <7% if diabetic)

INTRA-OPERATIVE MEASURES:

☐ Surgical hand antisepsis (proper technique) ☐ Sterile gowns and gloves
☐ Sterile drapes (incise drapes for high-risk cases) ☐ Maintain sterile field integrity
☐ Skin prep with appropriate agent:
- Chlorhexidine-alcohol ☐ Iodine-alcohol ☐ Iodophor ☐ Other: _________
☐ Allow adequate drying time (___ minutes)
☐ Normothermia maintenance (core temp >36°C)
☐ Glucose control (keep <180 mg/dL)
☐ Minimize OR traffic (door openings)
☐ Wound protectors for abdominal cases
☐ Antibiotic redosing for prolonged cases (q4h or 2x half-life)

POST-OPERATIVE MEASURES:

☐ Sterile dressing for 24-48 hours ☐ Proper hand hygiene before wound care
☐ Glucose control continued ☐ Discontinue antibiotics within 24 hours (unless indicated)
☐ Remove drains as soon as clinically indicated ☐ Patient/family education on wound care
